Convert country codes between COW and Gleditsch-Ward, by year

Source: R/utils.R
convert_state_code.Rd

countrycode maps codes one to one, without regard to the year, and has no equivalent for several states. This function handles the cases where the two systems differ:

  • Germany: COW 255 is GW 255 up to 1945 and GW 260 from 1946; COW 260 (German Federal Republic) is GW 260.

  • Serbia and Yugoslavia: COW 345 throughout; GW 340 (Serbia) up to 1915 and from June 2006, 345 (Yugoslavia) in between.

  • Czechoslovakia and the Czech Republic: GW 315 up to 1992, 316 from 1993.

  • Yemen: COW 678 (Yemen Arab Republic) up to 1990 and 679 (Yemen) from 1991; GW 678 throughout.

  • Vietnam: 816 in both systems (countrycode gives GW 815, a 19th-century state).

  • Microstates numbered differently: Kiribati (COW 946, GW 970), Nauru (970, 971), Tonga (955, 972), Tuvalu (947, 973).

Other codes that exist in both systems' state lists keep their number; the rest go through countrycode.

Usage

convert_state_code(code, year, from, to, month = NULL)

Arguments

code

Integer vector of codes.

year

Integer vector of years, recycled to code.

from, to

"cow" or "gw".

month

Optional integer vector of months, used for the 2006 split of Serbia and Montenegro (GW 340 from June 2006). Without it, all of 2006 is GW 340.

Value

An integer vector of codes in to; NA where there is no equivalent.

Details

The COW codes returned follow the package's COW panels, which code West Germany as 255 and Czechoslovakia as 316 (see standardize_cow()).
